title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
hook: Cramming a whole sentence into one vector loses information. This 2014 paper let the decoder look back at relevant source words at each step — the original attention mechanism.
key_points: Introduced attention: the decoder learns to focus on relevant parts of the input at each output step.
Removed the fixed-vector bottleneck that limited basic encoder–decoder models.
Improved translation quality, especially on longer sentences.
Produces soft alignments between source and target words as a byproduct.
Seeded the core idea that Transformers later built on.
content_html: Bahdanau, Cho, and Bengio fixed the biggest weakness of encoder–decoder translation: forcing the whole source sentence through a single fixed-length vector. Their answer was attention — letting the decoder dynamically look back at the most relevant input words as it produces each output word. It is the mechanism the entire Transformer era was built on.
extra_html:
How it works

Instead of relying on one summary vector, the encoder keeps a representation for every input word. At each decoding step, the model computes a set of weights scoring how relevant each input word is to the word being generated, then blends those representations into a context vector tailored to that step. Because the weights are learned end to end, the model figures out for itself which source words to align with each target word.

Why it matters

Attention lifted the information bottleneck and notably improved translation of long sentences, where the fixed-vector approach faltered. More importantly, it introduced the idea that a model can selectively focus on parts of its input — the seed that grew into self-attention and the Transformer architecture powering modern language models.

related.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning
related.hook: Translate a sentence by reading it into one vector, then writing a new sentence out of that vector. This encoder–decoder recipe powered early neural machine translation.

related.title: What Is Attention?
related.hook: Attention lets a model decide what to focus on: it scores how relevant each piece of input is to the current question, then blends them by those scores.

related.title: Attention Is All You Need
related.hook: Drop recurrence and convolution, keep only attention — and you get a model that trains in parallel and powers nearly every LLM since.
